analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, documentation only. I reviewed the head text (lines 791-1256) and the visible patch hunk. The patch retitles the candidate section to v0.10.1 and adds rollout notes. No source, configuration, workflow or authorization code is in these units, so no executable behavior changed. The changelog entries describe earlier releases: dev-build identity, fan helper v2 leases, App Attest worker, endpoint resumption and logout revocation, automatic release registration, SSD cache write budgets and external cache storage, account erasure, and so on. They record behavior already shipped or described elsewhere, and I did not treat them as new changes in this PR. Relevant threat IDs are T-041 (cache storage and the retained 30-minute TTL), T-053/T-054 (endpoint resumption, release qualification), T-044 to T-047 (fan helper) and A-008 (logout). The changelog language is consistent with those models and reaffirms the limits they state: no local trust is granted, Apple proof lifetimes are not extended, and only HTTP 204 confirms remote revocation. Candidate rollout notes in the patch excerpt say the matching platform change (darkbloom-platform#411) must be deployed first, which is a coordinator-side contract outside the supplied evidence. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and the head range 11-138 is only partly visible here, so the later lines of the new v0.10.1 section were not examined. I cannot verify that the claimed behavior (GLM logprob refusal, page-cache accounting changes affecting memory admission) is implemented as described. The memory-accounting change could alter admission and availability, but the code is not provided, so it is flagged for the next pass instead of reported as a finding. No concrete security regression is supported by this evidence.
